title: So the world has a beginning — made by the eternal mind we call God
source_text: XXX. Quum igitur nec motus nec tempus ab aeterno esse potuerint, sed necessario sui quoddam initium habeant: manifestum est mundum, qui, ut diximus, est in perpetuo motu, & cujus duratio tempore mensuratur, ab aeterno quoque esse non potuisse, sed aliquod sui initium habere; ac proinde illum ab alio factum esse & productum. Quis autem tanti operis author censeri poterit, nisi causa quaedam non tantum potentissima, sed etiam optima & sapientissima, adeoque nisi summa & aeterna quaedam mens, quae ab omnibus Dei nomine significatur?
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore neither motion nor time could be from eternity, but necessarily have some beginning of themselves: it is plain that the world, which as we said is in perpetual motion, and whose duration is measured by time, likewise could not be from eternity, but has some beginning of itself; and therefore was made and produced by another. But who can be judged the author of so great a work, unless some cause not only most powerful, but also best and most wise — and so unless some highest and eternal mind, which by all is signified by the name of God?
pass_b_english: Motion and time need a start — so the moving timed world does too.
Therefore the world was made by another.
Author: highest eternal mind — what all call God.

choices.term: nisi summa & aeterna quaedam mens, quae ab omnibus Dei nomine significatur
choices.english: unless some highest and eternal mind, which by all is signified by the name of God
choices.why: Names God as world's author after time/motion proofs.
rejected: world can be beginningless without God
